review.overall_assessment: The diagram captures the basic peering trigger flow and mediator handoff, but it still misses one required traffic-surge resource-supply behavior and contains some over-broad tracing that weakly suggests unsupported semantics.

defects.description: Requirement R89 is still not represented by any diagram node or edge.
defects.evidence: R89 requires that, in the face of traffic surges, information on available local resources along with their IDs is supplied to the Mediator. The current diagram only includes triggering the initiation request and the Mediator receiving it; it never models supplying local resource information or its IDs.
defects.suggested_action: Add a node/edge sequence that sends the available local resource information and IDs to the Mediator, or otherwise trace R89 to an explicit existing action if it is meant to be covered elsewhere.

strengths: The main trigger condition is modeled as a decision leading to sending an initiation request.
The Mediator receives the initiation request, matching the handoff required by the module.
The non-trigger path ends at a final node labeled as passing control to the next module, consistent with the self-contained module requirement.
